PC-OTH-014.explanation: Fair Access to Insurance Requirements plans are residual market associations, set up by law and funded by insurers, that provide basic property insurance to owners who cannot buy it in the voluntary market. Automobile assigned risk plans serve high-risk drivers.

PC-AUTO-001.explanation: Part A pays damages the insured owes to others and defends suits. Part B covers medical payments (in Texas, personal injury protection is also provided unless rejected in writing), Part C uninsured and underinsured motorists, and Part D damage to the auto.

excluded.PC-POL-024: Refund basis on insurer cancellation is set by Texas forms and TDI rules, not a general pro rata/short rate rule; TDI says the company refunds unearned premium within 15 days whoever cancels. Not asserted.
excluded.PC-POL-025: Short-rate refund on insured cancellation is not the rule on Texas personal lines forms (TDI guide shows a straight unearned-premium refund); excluded to avoid teaching a wrong Texas answer.
excluded.PC-AUTO-002: ISO PAP supplementary-payment dollar figure; the Texas Personal Auto Policy is a TDI-promulgated form and its figures were not verified.
excluded.PC-AUTO-003: ISO PAP loss-of-earnings dollar figure; not verified against the Texas PAP.
excluded.PC-AUTO-014: ISO PAP 14-day newly acquired auto window; not verified against the Texas PAP.
excluded.PC-AUTO-015: Says UM pays bodily injury only; Texas UM/UIM (TIC 1952.101) also covers property damage, so the key is incomplete in Texas.
excluded.PC-AUTO-018: Stacking item keys 'varies by state'; a Texas form should give the Texas answer, and that rule was not verified in current text, so the item is dropped.
excluded.PC-AUTO-022: ISO PAP transportation expense dollar figures; not verified against the Texas PAP.
excluded.PC-AUTO-030: ISO PAP cancellation reasons differ from TIC 551.104 (Texas allows cancellation for a fraudulent claim or legal violation, not misrepresentation on the application after 60 days).
excluded.PC-LIA-019: Exclusive remedy framed as universal; in Texas coverage is elective (Labor Code 406.002), so it applies only to subscribing employers. Covered by state items instead.
